# STUR Physics Lab: one simulation. Information for AI and LLM readers.

> The repository holds one script, production_v2_2.py: Python 3.8+, standard library
> only, with nothing tuned and nothing fitted. Measured inputs (PDG 2024, Planck 2018,
> CODATA, SI) are in INPUTS. Measured results used only for judging are in COMPARISONS.
> Numerical settings are in NUMERICS. Everything else is calculated. A test fails if a
> non-integer number appears outside those tables.

## What it computes
- Cosmology (flat LambdaCDM): Omega_r from T_CMB and N_eff, Omega_Lambda from flatness,
  age 13.795 Gyr (Planck: 13.787 +/- 0.020), q0, z_acc = 0.631, z_eq, horizon entropies.
- Quark flavour: quark masses run with the RG (two-loop QCD, one-loop QED, one-loop SM
  Yukawa/gauge above m_t) to 1.5-10 TeV, put into the Fritzsch six-zero texture, and
  diagonalized exactly. The two free phases are scanned over [0, 2pi).
- Result: |V_us|, |V_ub| and J are inside their bands. |V_cb| (32 sigma), |V_ub/V_cb|
  (14 sigma) and |V_td/V_ts| (5 sigma) are outside for every phase, so the six-zero
  texture is excluded.

- Texture survey: all 1,000 pairs of Hermitian quark mass matrices with 5 or 6 zeros
  (188 classes). 83 make predictions; 82 are excluded, and one survives (up 00X/0XX/XXX,
  down Fritzsch 0X0/X0X/0XX; chi^2 = 0.3 for 1 dof). No unknown is fixed: the band test is
  exact, and the joint test only decides survival.
- 3-3-1 (beta = +-1/sqrt3): every mass-matrix entry is gauge-allowed, so 3-3-1 forces no
  texture zero. The triplet family makes the survivor three distinct 3-3-1 hypotheses.

- Flavour symmetry (Part E): with the minimal 3-3-1 scalars, no abelian Z_N (N <= 6, exhaustive)
  makes a texture zero that keeps three-family mixing. Hermitian matrices cannot come from a
  symmetry commuting with SU(3)_L. Z_6 with 6 scalar triplets gives the survivor's zeros, but as
  general matrices they have 14 parameters for 10 observables (-4 predictions). Conclusion: no
  flavour symmetry inside 3-3-1 makes the survivor predictive.

- Closure (Part F): all 61,009 zero-pattern pairs of general quark mass matrices (497 classes).
  Exact Jacobian ranks of 10 weak-basis invariants: every pattern with three-family mixing and
  CP violation has exactly 10 physical parameters, so none predicts anything. Inside 3-3-1 the
  quark sector closes with 10 measured inputs (6 masses, 4 CKM parameters).
- Part G: the same in the Standard Model (general zeros, Part F) and in left-right models
  (parallel Hermitian textures; all 3 predictive ones excluded at >= 31 sigma). Texture zeros
  calculate no CKM number in any of the three frameworks.

- Part H (quantum and gravity, established physics): Planck units; the one-loop correction to
  Newton's law (41/(10 pi), quoted); Hawking, de Sitter and Unruh temperatures; gravity-mediated
  entanglement (smallest mass gravity can ever entangle maximally: (pi hbar^2/(G c t0))^(1/3) =
  89 MeV, same combination as Weinberg's pion relation; zero if gravity is classical); the
  proton/Planck hierarchy from logarithmic running. Exact identities: alpha_G = (m_p/M_P)^2,
  S_dS * rho_Lambda/rho_P = 3/8.

- Part I (alpha): grand unification at two loops from alpha_s and sin^2 theta_W. SM cannot
  unify (needs 1/alpha = 81.8 vs 127.95). In the MSSM, alpha is a function of the unknown
  superpartner scale; the measured value points to M_S ~ 2.5 TeV. Closed formulas for 1/alpha
  (Eddington, Wyler, 4pi^3+pi^2+pi) are excluded by >= 4000 sigma.

- Part J (Yukawas): SU(5) m_s/m_d = m_mu/m_e off by 558 sigma; Georgi-Jarlskog off by 10 sigma.
  b-tau unification fails in the SM (0.59-0.70); in the MSSM (scales from Part I) it needs
  tan(beta) = 1.35, and the top quasi-fixed point needs 1.33-1.40. No Yukawa is calculated.
- Part K (Higgs mass, MSSM): with Part I's M_S and Part J's tan(beta), maximal stop mixing gives m_h <= 103.9 GeV vs measured 125.20; that MSSM route is excluded.
- Part L (SM criticality): lambda(M_P) = 0, two-loop running, one-loop matching to pole masses, predicts M_h = 129.0 +/- 0.9 GeV vs 125.20 (matching shifts it +0.04 GeV); with lambda = beta_lambda = 0, M_t = 173.5 GeV. Measured M_h gives lambda(M_P) = -0.012.
- Every scale comes from the algorithm: m_t(m_t), Part I's M_S = 2.54 TeV and M_GUT, M_Planck.

## Files
- production_v2_2.py: the simulation
- results/production_v2_2.txt: expected output
- tests/test_production.py: the no-tuning rule and the pinned numbers
- archive/: notes and the 3-3-1 paper from the earlier codebase
